Court and police data shipped with the package

Source: R/justice.R
justice-data.Rd

Small excerpts of published court and police statistics, in inst/extdata, used by the examples, tests and the courts-and-crime vignette. Each is a faithful copy of published numbers (no value altered, no row invented); the full tables, every edition and location, are on the package's data hub (dload, collections ocj_statistics and tps_open_data).

Source

Ontario Court of Justice, court statistics, https://www.ontariocourts.ca/ocj/statistics/ (retrieved 2026-10-13), editions 2012 to 2026, published by the Court for public use. Toronto Police Service, Public Safety Data Portal, dataset “Break and Enter Open Data”, https://data.tps.ca/ (retrieved 2026-10-13); contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence - Toronto Police Service. See inst/COPYRIGHTS.

Value

No R object: each file is a CSV in inst/extdata. Read one into a data frame with read.csv() on the path that system.file("extdata", <file>, package = "rmoriebricklayer") gives.

Details

ocj_flow_ontario.csv

Ontario Court of Justice, criminal clearance-rate statistics, province-wide, monthly from April 2024 to March 2026 (the 2026 edition): month, cases received, cases disposed, cases pending (net of bench warrants).

ocj_time_to_disposition.csv

The same months from the disposition-rate statistics: the shares of cases disposed in under 10 months, 10-15, 15-18 and over 18 months (cases without bench warrants), and the average days to disposition.

ocj_dispositions.csv

Province-wide criminal cases disposed by how they ended, one row per calendar year 2012-2019, 2021, 2022, 2024 and 2025; each row adds to the year's published total. The 2020 edition covers October to September and the 2026 edition April to March; the 2023 edition publishes no Toronto figures, so it has no province-wide row.

ocj_offence_groups.csv

The same years by offence group: cases received and disposed. The groups add to each year's province-wide total.

ocj_courts.csv

The same years by court, with court_series, which names Toronto's courthouses "Toronto" throughout: from 2023 the Court publishes Toronto as one location (the new Toronto courthouse consolidated its criminal courts that year). Each year's courts add to the province-wide total.

tps_break_enter_d14_2024.csv

Toronto Police Service Break and Enter open data, every break and enter that occurred in 2024 in division D14, one row per occurrence (508): event_id, occurrence date, premises type, the published longitude and latitude (which the Service offsets to the nearest intersection), and offence_records, the number of offence records the Service publishes for the occurrence (five have two). The source package builds it with the script tps_break_enter_d14_2024.R in its data-raw folder.

See also

caseflow, lifetbl, dispmix, clrdcmp, crmdens, knoxtst.

Examples

f <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "ocj_flow_ontario.csv",
                          package = "rmoriebricklayer"))
head(f)
#>     month received disposed pending
#> 1 2024-04    21265    22053  148904
#> 2 2024-05    21521    22546  147957
#> 3 2024-06    19728    20599  145989
#> 4 2024-07    22483    19552  147277
#> 5 2024-08    21019    18383  149417
#> 6 2024-09    20720    18186  151588
c <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "ocj_courts.csv",
                          package = "rmoriebricklayer"))
tapply(c$disposed, c$year, sum)
#>   2012   2013   2014   2015   2016   2017   2018   2019   2021   2022   2023 
#> 247047 231681 210098 205249 207160 214137 211488 220548 204308 209961 203206 
#>   2024   2025 
#> 245160 245012
